thread.title: Stocks Surge At Open; Dow Jones Fights To Extend Rally | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Surge At Open; Dow Jones Fights To Extend Rally | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks bolted higher at Friday's open, hoisted by earnings reports and rising global markets, as the Dow Jones Industrial Average sought to add a fifth straight week to the market's rally.
X Some of the biggest early gains came from Western Digital ( WDC ), Seagate Technology ( STX ) and Starbucks ( SBUX ). Chip stocks were sharply mixed after rallying Thursday , as Dow Jones stock Intel ( INTC ) tanked following mixed fourth-quarter results , but Micron Technology ( MU ) and STMicroelectronics ( STM ) posted strong premarket gains.
Makers of medical devices took some hard early hits , as Resmed ( RMD ) and Intuitive Surgical ( ISRG ) dived on earnings results.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average muscled up 0.9%. Intel dragged hard on the Dow's early action, while DowDupont ( DWDP ) and Apple ( AAPL ) powered up more than 2% apiece.
The S&P 500 jumped 0.8%, led by Western Digital, Seagate Technology and Starbucks. Medical products maker Resmed dived to the bottom of the list following a mixed quarterly report.

Dow Jones: Can It Extend Rally To Fifth Week? Thursday's choppy action handed the Dow Jones Industrial Average its second loss for the week and left it facing its first weekly decline of the year. The index was down 0.6% through Thursday. It was holding above its 50-day moving average — a positive — but remained hung up not quite 2% below the 25,000 level.
The Nasdaq and S&P 500 both gained ground on Thursday. But the S&P 500 ended the session down 1.1% so far for the week, with the Nasdaq shouldering a 1.2% loss. Like the Dow, both indexes are tracking toward their first weekly decline since the week ended Dec. 21.
Shutdown: 34 Days Two competing bills attempting to end the shutdown of federal offices and operations failed on votes in the Senate on Thursday. But as the shutdown enters its 35th day, senators were reportedly engaged at new levels, working to craft a compromise between the White House and House Democrat positions. House Democrats were reportedly attempting to finalize a new border security plan.
A Senate effort to reopen federal offices for a three-week period in which negotiations would continue reportedly failed, as the White House demanded that the proposal must include an up-front payment on a wall along the southern U.S. border. President Trump is demanding $5.7 billion for a wall and other border security measures. Democrats refuse to fund such a wall.
JPMorgan economists on Thursday trimmed their first-quarter growth forecasts for the second time in two weeks, as impact from the shutdown continues to compile. The report trimmed the first-quarter growth outlook to 1.75% , down from a prior estimate of 2%. It raised its second-quarter growth outlook to 2.25%, from 2%, allowing for a bounce back, assuming federal offices reopen.
The Commerce Department will not report December durable goods orders or new homes sales data today due to the shutdown.
Dow Jones Stock: Intel Crumbles Intel tumbled nearly 7% after its fourth-quarter revenue rose less than expected. Earnings beat analyst estimates , but first-quarter and full-year guidance was soft. Intel closed Thursday up almost 17% from an October low, and building the right side of a possible seven-month base pattern. Friday's action implied the stock would open back below its 10-week moving average . Not all premarket action carries over into regular trade.
Starbucks Nears Buy Point IBD 50 stock Starbucks banged a gain of nearly 4%, after reporting late Thursday an across-the-board beat for its fiscal first quarter . Earnings, revenue and same-store sales all topped expectations, and management hoisted its full-year profit guidance to above analyst targets.
The advance put the stock, also on the IBD Leaderboard list of premium stocks, less than 3% below a 69.08 flat-base buy point .
Western Digital, Seagate Technology Soar Western Digital vaulted 9% higher, as the data storage leader announced plans to trim costs following weaker-than-forecast fiscal second-quarter earnings late Thursday. A 21% decline in revenue was in line with expectations. Management said it expected to see strengthening sales in the second half of the year. Stifel Nicolaus also trimmed the stock's price target to 48, from 60, early Friday.
The updraft lifted data storage peer Seagate Technology, which jumped more than 8% in early trade. Seagate is scheduled to report its second-quarter results on Feb. 2. Both Western and Seagate have been rebounding since late December, but remain deep in 10-month corrections.
China Gets Bank Boost; Frankfurt, Paris Rally Markets in China and Japan popped Friday after Chinese regulators announced measures broadening the bond market for banks, giving them increased access to capital and making their stock shares more attractive. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rallied 1.7%, to end up 1.9% in its fourth straight weekly advance — its longest runup since January 2018. The Shanghai Composite rose 0.4%.
In Japan, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 seized a 1% gain, leaving the benchmark ahead 0.5% for the week to end in a test of its 50-day moving average.
Stocks in Europe picked up on optimism in Asia and the U.S., rallying ahead of the U.K. in afternoon trade. Frankfurt's DAX led, up 1.5%. The CAC-40 in Paris gained 1%. In London, the FTSE 100 managed a 0.2% advance.
ResMed Set To Trigger Sell Rule Sleep aid products maker ResMed collapsed nearly 17% lower as JPMorgan downgraded the stock after its report late Thursday showed fiscal second-quarter revenue growth stopped well sort of analyst expectations. Earnings easily cleared the consensus target as gross margins expanded 70 basis points.
ResMed shares had just cleared a 116.42 buy point in a cup-with-handle base. Friday's early action sent the stock back below its 10-week moving average and more than 8% below the base's buy point, triggering the automatic sell rule .
